grow.insight.title: Insight of the day
grow.insight.1: Recognising a page is not the same as remembering it. Close the book and see what you can recall.
grow.insight.2: Pulling an answer out of memory strengthens it far more than reading it again.
grow.insight.3: A little forgetting between reviews is useful: the effort of remembering again makes the memory last longer.
grow.insight.4: Spread your reviews out over days and weeks. The same minutes in one sitting are forgotten faster.
grow.insight.5: If a method feels hard but you remember more the next day, that is a desirable difficulty, not a failure.
grow.insight.6: Sleep moves the day’s learning into longer-lasting memory. An all-nighter skips that step.
grow.insight.7: Try a question before you learn the answer. Even a wrong guess helps the right answer stick.
grow.insight.8: Mixing different kinds of problems feels slower, but it teaches you to choose the right approach, which is what exams ask.
grow.insight.9: Asking “why is this true?” ties a new fact to what you already know.
grow.insight.10: If you can’t explain it in plain words, you’ve found a gap. That is the best moment to learn.
grow.insight.11: Just expecting to teach something makes you organise it better and remember more.
grow.insight.12: Words plus a simple sketch give your memory two ways in.
grow.insight.13: Two examples from different contexts help an idea travel to problems you haven’t seen yet.
grow.insight.14: Judge a new method after about five sessions, not one. Every new method feels awkward at first.
grow.insight.15: Rate your recall the next day. The warm glow right after studying is a poor guide to what you’ll keep.
grow.insight.16: Change one thing at a time, so you know what made the difference.
grow.insight.17: The best method scores well on recall and on enjoyment, because it is the one you will keep using.
grow.insight.18: Missing one day doesn’t undo a habit. Restart at the next small landmark: tomorrow, Monday, the next chapter.
grow.insight.19: A new habit takes weeks to months to feel automatic, about two months on average. Be patient with yourself.
grow.insight.20: Writing your worries down for a few minutes before studying frees up room in working memory.
grow.insight.21: A long, slow breath out works like a brake for a stressed body.
grow.insight.22: A racing heart before an exam can be your body getting ready. Energy, not danger.
grow.insight.23: Talk to yourself the way you’d talk to a friend. A missed day is data, not a verdict.
grow.insight.24: Compare yourself with last week’s you. That is a fair race.
grow.insight.25: Decide what a finished day looks like, then stop when you get there.
grow.insight.26: Rest you planned is recovery, not slacking. It protects the long game.
grow.insight.27: Most of the dread sits before a task, not inside it. Promise yourself just five minutes.
grow.insight.28: Make the next step absurdly small: not “study chemistry” but “open lecture 4 and read the first slide”.
grow.insight.29: Songs with lyrics compete with reading for the same mental resources. Silence or instrumental music is easier.
grow.insight.30: Start a topic with a puzzle. Curiosity puts your brain in a ready-to-learn state.
grow.insight.31: Hours studied is a poor measure of progress. What you can recall without notes is a better one.
grow.insight.32: A done list shows what you did, not only what is left. It quiets the “I did nothing today” story.

grow.lab.title: Method Lab
grow.lab.lede: Try one method for 1–2 weeks, rate each session, then keep, tweak or drop it.
grow.lab.empty: No experiment running. Pick a method you’re curious about.
grow.lab.baselineHint: Tip: run “my usual way” alongside it, so you have something to compare with.
grow.lab.how.1: Change one thing: pick one method and keep your time and place about the same.
grow.lab.how.2: Give it at least 5 sessions over 1–2 weeks. New methods feel awkward at first.
grow.lab.how.3: After each session, tap enjoyment, focus and effort. The next day, quiz yourself for 2 minutes and rate recall.
grow.lab.how.4: Then decide: keep, tweak or drop.
grow.lab.oneThing: Change just this one thing. Keep your study time and place about the same.
grow.lab.newLede: Treat it like a small, friendly science project about you.
grow.lab.rateLede: Three quick taps. Tomorrow you’ll rate how much you recall.
grow.lab.judgeAfter.one: Judge it after 5 sessions: {n} to go.
grow.lab.judgeAfter.few: Judge it after 5 sessions: {n} to go.
grow.lab.judgeAfter.many: Judge it after 5 sessions: {n} to go.
grow.lab.judgeAfter.other: Judge it after 5 sessions: {n} to go.
grow.lab.recallAsk: Quiz yourself for 2 minutes on what you studied on {date}. How much did you recall?
grow.lab.effortNote: High effort isn’t bad: effortful methods often work best.
grow.lab.recallLater: Recall is rated the day after each session.
grow.lab.suggest.keep: 💚 Good recall and you enjoy it. A strong candidate to keep.
grow.lab.suggest.tweak: 🔧 It works, but it feels like a chore. Keep it and change the format: shorter sessions, a study partner, a different place.
grow.lab.suggest.dropWarmup: 🍂 Fun, but recall is low. Drop it as a main method; keep it as a warm-up if you like it.
grow.lab.suggest.drop: 🍂 Low recall and low enjoyment. Drop it without guilt and try something else.
grow.lab.suggest.few: Only a few ratings so far, so trust your gut here.
grow.lab.notePlaceholder: For example: works for vocabulary, try 15-minute blocks
grow.lab.decided: Decision saved. You know yourself a bit better now ✨
grow.lab.betterThis: Recall is higher with this one so far.
grow.lab.betterOther: Recall is higher with the other one so far.
grow.lab.similar: Recall is about the same so far. Enjoyment can be the tie-breaker.

grow.profile.lede: What worked for you, built from your own experiments.
grow.profile.empty: Finish an experiment and your profile starts here.
grow.profile.monthly: Once a month, take a look here: what suits this course may change for the next.
grow.wins.title: Done list & wins
grow.wins.lede: Write down what you did, not only what’s left. Small things count.
grow.wins.label: What did you do?
grow.wins.empty: Nothing yet today. Even “opened my notes” counts.
grow.wins.noWins: No wins starred yet. Tap ☆ on anything you’re proud of.
grow.reflect.title: Weekly reflection
grow.reflect.lede: Ten calm minutes. No blame, just notes for next week.
grow.reflect.slipped.hint: Too ambitious, bad timing, tired… it’s data, not a verdict.
grow.calm.title: Calm corner
grow.calm.lede: For when worry takes up the room you need for thinking.
grow.calm.note: These are self-help habits for everyday study stress, not treatment. If anxiety or low mood lasts for weeks, please talk to someone.
grow.worry.title: Worry dump
grow.worry.short: Write it down, then put it away
grow.worry.lede: For a few minutes, write whatever is worrying you. Spelling and logic don’t matter.
grow.worry.label: Your worries
grow.worry.private: 🔒 Nobody will read it. It isn’t saved anywhere.
grow.worry.doneText: Your head has a little more room now. Start with the first small task.
grow.breathe.title: Breathe
grow.breathe.short: A calm minute with a slow breath out
grow.breathe.lede: Follow the circle. Make the breath out longer than the breath in.
grow.breathe.p.446.hint: In for 4, hold for 4, out for 6.
grow.breathe.p.sigh.hint: Two breaths in through the nose, one long breath out. A quick reset.
grow.breathe.p.46.hint: In for 4, out for 6. Simple and steady.

grow.why.label: My why
grow.why.hint.2: What do you want to be able to do?
grow.why.hint.3: Who will it help, including future you?
grow.why.caption: Written by you, for the hard days.
